milestones.title: Megarian Greeks found Byzantion
milestones.detail: Settlers from Megara established a colony with an acropolis beside the Golden Horn. Ancient sources give dates between 667 and 657 BCE.

milestones.title: Septimius Severus besieges and rebuilds Byzantium
milestones.detail: Having backed the losing side in a Roman civil war, the city was besieged and badly damaged in 196. Severus then rebuilt it.

milestones.title: Constantinople dedicated as the Roman capital
milestones.detail: Constantine rebuilt and enlarged the city from 324 and inaugurated it as 'New Rome' on 11 May 330.
milestones.source: Barnes (1981), Constantine and Eusebius, pp. 212, 222, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul#Byzantine_era

milestones.title: Theodosian Walls completed
milestones.detail: A new land wall about 2 km west of Constantine's wall, finished in 413 according to the Codex Theodosianus, more than doubled the enclosed area to about 14 square kilometres.

milestones.title: Hagia Sophia consecrated
milestones.detail: The earlier cathedral burned down in the Nika revolt of January 532; Justinian I built the present domed basilica between 532 and 537.

milestones.title: Plague of Justinian
milestones.detail: The plague of 541-542 is said to have killed 20 to 40 per cent of the city's inhabitants, though some historians argue the toll was lower.

milestones.title: Fourth Crusade sacks the city
milestones.detail: Crusaders captured and pillaged Constantinople in April 1204 and set up the Latin Empire. The city was badly depopulated.
milestones.source: Gregory (2010), A History of Byzantium, pp. 324-333, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul#Byzantine_era

milestones.title: Byzantine rule restored
milestones.detail: The Byzantines recovered a city whose churches, defences and services were in disrepair and whose population had fallen to about a hundred thousand.
milestones.source: Gregory (2010), A History of Byzantium, pp. 340-342, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul#Byzantine_era

milestones.title: Ottoman conquest
milestones.detail: Mehmed II took the city on 29 May 1453 after a 55-day siege, made it the Ottoman capital and set about repopulating and rebuilding it.

milestones.title: Constantinople earthquake
milestones.detail: A major earthquake in 1509 destroyed more than a thousand houses and damaged the fortifications, including the Galata Tower; death-toll estimates range from 1,000 to 13,000.

milestones.title: Süleymaniye Mosque completed
milestones.detail: The mosque complex built for Suleiman the Magnificent on the site of the old Ottoman palace was completed in 1557, at the height of Ottoman building in the capital.

milestones.title: Great Fire of 1660
milestones.detail: The Great Fire of 24-26 July 1660 swept the city.

milestones.title: First Galata Bridge
milestones.detail: The first Galata Bridge was built in 1845, one of several bridges across the Golden Horn built in the reform era to join the old city to Galata.
milestones.source: Celik (1993), The Remaking of Istanbul, pp. 87-89, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Istanbul

milestones.title: Tünel underground railway opens
milestones.detail: The funicular between Karaköy and Beyoğlu opened on 17 January 1875. The city was linked to the European railway network in the 1880s.
milestones.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Istanbul ; Harter (2005), World Railways of the Nineteenth Century, p. 251, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul

milestones.title: Capital moves to Ankara
milestones.detail: The Turkish Republic was proclaimed on 29 October 1923 with Ankara as capital. By the 1927 census the municipality held about 691,000 people, little more than half its wartime peak.

milestones.title: Henri Prost's master plan
milestones.detail: Planning led by Henri Prost between 1936 and 1950 cut new boulevards, squares and parks through the historic fabric, including Taksim Square and Atatürk Boulevard.
milestones.source: Keyder (1999), Istanbul: Between the Global and the Local, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul#Turkish_Republic

milestones.title: Bosphorus Bridge opens
milestones.detail: The first bridge between the European and Asian sides was completed on 30 October 1973 and accelerated migration and the city's spread into Anatolia.

milestones.title: Istanbul Metro begins operating
milestones.detail: The M1 line opened on 3 September 1989, the first of a network that had ten lines by 2023.

milestones.title: İzmit earthquake
milestones.detail: The magnitude 7.6 earthquake of 17 August 1999 struck neighbouring Kocaeli Province and killed more than 17,000 people in the region.

milestones.title: Marmaray rail tunnel opens
milestones.detail: The rail tunnel under the Bosphorus opened on 29 October 2013, linking the European and Asian rail systems.

notes: Start date: the Greek colony of Byzantion is the city's first documented foundation, but its date is not agreed. Herodotus puts it 17 years after Chalcedon, which gives 667 BCE when Chalcedon is dated 685; Eusebius gives 659 or 656 BCE; some modern historians prefer the 640s or later. The file uses about 660 BCE and marks it 'estimated'. Neolithic remains at Yenikapı (6th millennium BCE) and a Thracian settlement (Lygos) on the same point are older but are not a continuous city. Population: there is no figure between the founding and 100 BCE, and none between 100 BCE and 400 CE (so the Severan destruction of 196 and the growth after 330 are not resolved). The medieval series is Chandler's; Modelski's estimates for 500-1000 are much higher (500,000-600,000) and Morris (2010) argues Chandler's are themselves too high, so the Byzantine peak is uncertain by a factor of about two. The declines after the plagues, after 1204 and to 1453 are recorded as Chandler gives them. Ottoman-era figures to 1850 are Chandler's estimates; 1885 is the first complete Ottoman census. Figures for 1885-1914 cover the city with its Bosphorus and Asian suburbs, while 1927 is the municipality only, which exaggerates the real post-war fall slightly. The Republican censuses of 1935, 1940 and 1945 could be found only as province totals (883,599, 991,237 and 1,078,399 on Wikipedia), so they are left out. Landmarks: mosque heights are minaret heights, with dome heights in the notes. Heights could not be sourced for Topkapı Palace, Rumeli Hisarı, the Maiden's Tower or Haydarpaşa station; the Yavuz Sultan Selim Bridge (322 m towers, 2016) is omitted because no coordinates were found on the pages consulted.
